steps.name: Sylvia
steps.text: ...Why is someone still outside this late?

steps.name: Sylvia
steps.text: Is that... Jessica?

steps.name: Sylvia
steps.text: What brings you here at this hour, Miss?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: I... *huff*, *huff* I... have some business here!

steps.name: Sylvia
steps.text: L-Let's... talk inside, shall we?

steps.name: Bank Manager
steps.text: What's going on, Sylvia? Didn't I tell you to keep the door closed at night? Recently those people from Blacksteel have been—

steps.name: Bank Manager
steps.text: Ah. So it was you, Miss.

steps.name: Bank Manager
steps.text: I'm not sure why you've paid us a visit at this hour, but how may I serve you?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Don't... don't chase them out!

steps.name: Bank Manager
steps.text: Chase them out? Who exactly?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: The residents with debt! Don't let Blacksteel drive them out!

steps.name: Bank Manager
steps.text: ...Who's this coming from? Mr. Cliff?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: I... it's from me!

steps.name: Bank Manager
steps.text: Did I hear that right? If this is a joke, I'm not sure I get it.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: I'm serious! If you need someone to pay off their debts, then I-I'll pay it off for them! At least enough to let them stay through winter? Sending them to the frontier now is no different from a death sentence!

spans.text: I'm serious! If you need someone to pay off their debts, then I-I'll pay it off for them! At least enough to let them stay through winter? Sending them to the frontier
is no different from a death sentence!

steps.name: Bank Manager
steps.text: What holds sway in a bank are not the delusions of a mercenary, but honest-to-goodness gold certificates.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: I have the certs! This isn't a crazy fantasy, I can walk the walk and pay off their debts!

steps.name: Bank Manager
steps.text: I'm sorry, but the bank doesn't have time to indulge your nonsense—

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: I'm the daughter of Bernie Brynley... The CEO and largest shareholder of Raythean Industries!
Jessica freezes on the spot as soon as she finishes speaking. Ever since she joined Blacksteel, she has never once relied on her father or her family to handle any setbacks she's faced.
This was her one unwavering insistence—she did not want any special treatment because of her family name.
But she had just unleashed the name of her father, as well as the one that sits on their family crest.

steps.name: Bank Manager
steps.text: Bernie Brynley?

steps.name: Bank Manager
steps.text: You must be quite the bigshot then, Miss Jessica Brynley.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Spare me the sarcasm, ma'am. Just give me the number.

steps.name: Bank Manager
steps.text: Hm... I can't give you an exact figure on the spot, but no matter. Sylvia is here, and she's always been good with numbers.

steps.name: Bank Manager
steps.text: What are you standing there for, Sylvia? Tell her.

steps.name: Sylvia
steps.text: ...Miss, I—

steps.name: Bank Manager
steps.text: She's a child of the Brynley family. It should be a paltry sum to her.

steps.name: Sylvia
steps.text: This, this isn't a good idea...

steps.name: Bank Manager
steps.text: Tell her, Sylvia!

steps.name: Sylvia
steps.text: Currently... everyone's debt in Davistown roughly totals to... 276 million certs. If we calculate the interest until spring, the amount you'll need is roughly...

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: How much?

steps.name: Sylvia
steps.text: 28,450,000 gold certificates.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Twenty-eight... million?

steps.name: Bank Manager
steps.text: A small price for three months of peace and stability on the plate, no?

steps.name: Bank Manager
steps.text: At a loss for words, Miss Brynley?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: I-I don't have that much on hand right now, b-but I can make the arrangements...

steps.name: Bank Manager
steps.text: 28,450,000... So even a trust fund heiress can't withdraw that much money in one go?

steps.name: Bank Manager
steps.text: I've learned something new today.

steps.name: Sylvia
steps.text: Jessica...

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Sylvia, I-I...

steps.name: Sylvia
steps.text: You're... you're not from Davistown. There's really... no need to do this for our sake.

steps.name: Sylvia
steps.text: Listen to me. You should just leave... E-Even if you have enough for this time, could you afford the next one? Or the one after that?
Jessica's lips tremble as she fails to let even a single word out.
She knows Sylvia is not being wry, but just stating the facts.
The long string of numbers in her account can ensure a carefree lifetime for her, but isn't enough to guarantee even a month's stability for the people of this plate.

spans.text: The long string of numbers in her account can ensure a carefree lifetime for
, but isn't enough to guarantee even a month's stability for the people of this plate.

steps.text: She thinks back to her father's earnest reminders—To always act within her means, and to weigh the pros and cons before doing so.
But she never learned to, and thus has no achievements to her name.

steps.name: Secretary
steps.text: Sir? Are you in there?

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: Yes. What's the matter?

steps.name: Secretary
steps.text: He's here. Is it a good time for you to meet?

steps.name: Secretary
steps.text: Sir?

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: Yes, I heard you. Bring him in.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Jessica? Ain't you supposed to be back on the Blacksteel landship?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: ...Helena, is Woodrow back yet?

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: No, he said he went out to see an old friend, and isn't back yet.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: You don't look so good... What's wrong? Did something happen to Woody?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: No... He must have gone to our landship to meet the boss. They're old friends, so... maybe he can change his mind.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: The boss of Blacksteel? He never told me he knew a bigshot like that.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Doesn't he have a photo of him and some other Sankta...?

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Photo? That rings a bell, but ain't it always locked away in his drawer? How did you manage a look?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: That... that's not important. What's important is that the three in the photo were all smiles, right?

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: ...Are you sure Woody went to look for the man in the photo?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: ...So you do know something about them?

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: I dunno much about Woody's time in the Revolutionary War, and even less about the people in that photo...

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: But back then, it was your boss who made the choice that led to Woody and the other man getting captured by the enemy and locked up in Camp Collus.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: ...Is that... an internment camp?

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: You didn't know? Well, it's ancient history. No official would ever bring it up, so of course you young'uns wouldn't know about it.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: It was a POW camp built by the Victorian Army during the Columbian Revolutionary War. And what went on in there was... appalling. I'm talking torture.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Torture...?!

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Yeah. For every ten that went in, only one made it out.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: So Jessica, who'd ever call someone who left them to rot in a place like that an old friend...?
Jessica recalls the brown identification document.
She suddenly realizes that the document's color was not just a random shade of brown, but the color of dried blood.
Sir, are you in there?

steps.name: Somber Mercenary
steps.text: Yes. What's the matter?
He's here, sir. Is it a good time for you to meet?

steps.name: Somber Mercenary
steps.text: Yes, just bring him in.

steps.name: Haggard Looking Man
steps.text: ...May I sit?

steps.name: Somber Mercenary
steps.text: Of course.

steps.name: Somber Mercenary
steps.text: We have chairs, Woody.

steps.name: Haggard Looking Man
steps.text: ...Sorry, got used to sitting on the ground these past two years. I forgot I can sit on chairs without... getting beat up.
Autumn 1019, Columbia, Camp Collus

steps.name: Haggard Looking Man
steps.text: ...Calling me here... Got something to say to me?

steps.name: Somber Mercenary
steps.text: I figured you'd be the one full of questions for me.

spans.text: I figured you'd be the one full of questions for

steps.name: Haggard Looking Man
steps.text: No, just the one.

steps.name: Haggard Looking Man
steps.text: Why didn't you back me up, three years ago?

steps.name: Somber Mercenary
steps.text: The situation changed after you left. Once the enemy encirclement suddenly tightened around our right flank, I had no choice but to abandon the original rescue plan and conserve our forces.

steps.name: Haggard Looking Man
steps.text: ...You're gonna write it off with just that understatement?

steps.name: Haggard Looking Man
steps.text: You devised a rescue plan, sent me as a decoy, and in the end, you didn't even rescue him.

steps.name: Somber Mercenary
steps.text: The circumstances compelled me to take responsibility for my men.

steps.name: Haggard Looking Man
steps.text: Don't give me that, with that face like you don't care!

steps.name: Somber Mercenary
steps.text: Why are you so obsessed with my expressions, Woody? You've been scrutinizing my face since the moment I stepped in.

steps.name: Somber Mercenary
steps.text: Since when did... Sankta ever need to pay attention to body language? What's going on, Woody?

steps.name: Haggard Looking Man
steps.text: ...It became a habit after he passed. After all, ain't no other Sankta in here.

steps.name: Somber Mercenary
steps.text: When did he die? The document only has one 'dead' stamped in here, and the rest aren't even recorded.

steps.name: Haggard Looking Man
steps.text: I can't remember the details... Didn't have a calendar or a watch... Probably last year? Early spring... no, summer. I saw a pansy outside the barbed-wired fence that day.

steps.name: Somber Mercenary
steps.text: What happened...?

steps.name: Haggard Looking Man
steps.text: At first... he was burning hot... He was mumbling non-stop, eyes wide open, and he was grabbing my sleeve like a lifeline. Like he wanted to tell me something.

steps.name: Haggard Looking Man
steps.text: So I moved closer, to make out what he was trying to say.

steps.name: Somber Mercenary
steps.text: And what was it...?

steps.name: Haggard Looking Man
steps.text: Dunno, didn't hear. He let go of my sleeve, his eyes still open, pupils all dilated... Pitch-black... like they could suck in everything around him.

steps.name: Somber Mercenary
steps.text: Woody...

steps.name: Haggard Looking Man
steps.text: So why... why... why didn't you come?

a.text: The man turns his head, and with a blank stare returns the mercenary's gaze.
The black of his pupils incessantly spreads, circulates, and rotates, as if trying to swallow up everything in the surroundings.
As the mercenary faces the other man's glare, he feels as if a hook has extended from out of nowhere, piercing through his ankle and relentlessly dragging him into that black vortex.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: So what do I call you now? Heard you go by a different name.

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: Anything's fine... I was expecting you sooner, Woody.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: After what happened last night, I had so many things on my plate and so many friends to help out.

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: If you need any help, you can always let me know. Be it cash or manpower.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Thanks, Cliff, but no thanks. Help is only help when it's on time. But coming from you... it's always overdue.

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: Right. It's always best to get things done in a timely manner.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: So what are you doing here?

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: Can't an old friend start with a 'how do you do'?

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: ...It's not as simple as 'old friends' between us. What made you think we'd be acting like friends when we saw each other again?

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: Then what would you rather be treated as?

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Anything else, really.

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: No need for sarcasm, Woody. I don't even see the point anymore. We're old now, our hair's gone full white.

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: This past decade, I've seen my friends getting one health problem after another, and been attending funeral after funeral. Just meeting one that's still alive is hard enough.

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: You live so far away, and I doubt I'll ever see your obituary in the papers, so I came see you personally.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: You shouldn't have bothered. Ain't no place for you at my funeral anyhow.

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: That's a real shame, Woody. Didn't we make that pact to speak at each other's funerals, all those years ago?

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: I'm sure plenty of others would be happy for you to speak at theirs, but mine... just forget about it.

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: I hope you're not thinking I'm a fan of funerals. I only attend them because it's my old buddies in the coffins.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: And where do you sit? Among the friends and family?

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: Rarely. Unless their relatives ask me to, I usually stand back and watch the whole thing from a distance.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Why? Afraid you can't bear their pain?

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: Pain is a relatively private experience for the other races. My best guess is that we can only deal with it on our own.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Enough playing like we're friends, alright? I'll put it bluntly for you—I buried him on the hillside behind the POW camp. Have you ever visited him?

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: Unfortunately, no. I haven't found the time.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: ...You haven't changed a bit.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: So why would Woody go looking for him...?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: It's my fault... I asked him to.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: What?! You?!

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: I thought... on account of their past friendship, maybe my boss could be more... lenient on everyone here.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: How could you be so naive? Jessica... Woody, he...

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Forget it. Now that it's come to this, I don't need to hide it from you.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: I'm planning to leave this plate and head to the frontier.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: You too...?

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Yeah, my regulars are all getting sent off one after the other, and only us old folks are left. What's the point in keeping the diner open?

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Besides, just look at the holes in my walls, after last night's fighting. I don't have it in me to patch 'em up anymore.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: I've invested so many years into this place... and enough is enough.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Sorry... I'm so sorry...

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: What're you apologizing for, Jessica?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Because I didn't do anything. Nothing at all. I'm sorry, I really am...

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Don't blame yourself. You're the last person who should be doing that. You're an outsider, and the plate was on its last legs. Just get back to your friends.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: You have your own life to live. No need to work yourself to the bone on our account.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: And the check you gave me back then... Take it back.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: But... that's the only thing I can do for you...

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Take it.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: ...When do you plan to leave, Helena?

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Not too soon, I reckon. Still have to say my proper goodbyes, after all.
Jessica shuts the restaurant door behind her and stands in a daze on the doorstep, the check balled up in her fist.
She suddenly lets loose a kick on a pile of snow by the road, sprinkling flakes of white down onto her head and wetting her hair. Some land on her forehead, cooling her burning heat.
She retrieves a tape recorder from her bag and begins rewinding it, playing back the recording she has heard so many times.

a.text: '...But you're just a naive little heiress. What can you even do?'

steps.text: This thought fills her mind as she walks slowly back towards the giant black landship.
...Anyone hear that?
Save us... Those, those Sarkaz suddenly climbed up the plate...
Many people are dead, and the rest of us are hiding in the basement of City Hall... *bzzt*... *bzzt*...
We tried to contact Londinium's garrisons...
But no one's replied... no one at all...
I don't care who it is, but if you can hear this message, please, help us...
You're our only hope...
*bzzt*... *bzzt*...
Why did I even want to be a mercenary?
I can't save other people's lives, or even their livelihoods.

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: Where have you been all day, Jessica? We couldn't get in touch.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: I went... It's nothing, I just went for a walk.

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: What happened?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Captain, I... I... really have no idea why we're doing this mission.

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: Did... you see something?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: ...I saw our colleagues evicting debt-saddled residents from their homes, and putting them on convoys bound for the frontier.

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: Hey, Teacher's Pet, now's not the time to be staring at your communicator!

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: Did you even hear what she said?!

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: I did... and I have news even more absurd than that.

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: Orders from above: we'll be in charge of security at the bank. We have to stand watch 24/7, and it's up to us to figure out our shift rotation.

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: What...? Working security for the bank?!

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: Correct.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Hah...

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: ... This is so... goddamn... ridiculous...

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: Jessica, you...
